subject: Cache feedback loop causing 504s at Orchid Labs
body:
From: support@orchidlabs.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:14:23 -0700
Subject: High 504s starting 06/01 - will need urgent help

Hi Connor,

We started seeing a large uptick in 504 gateway timeouts across our API surface at ~07:50 PDT this morning. The errors correlate with a sudden rise in per-request latency and a sharp increase in retry attempts on the client side. Attaching a screenshot of our SRE dashboard (orchid_504_spike.png) and a short trace excerpt (svc_trace_excerpt.txt).

Sample symptom summary:
- Error rate: 504s and 5xx spiked from ~0.2% to 8% in 10 minutes
- Latency tail (p99) jumped from 120ms to 3.2s
- Retry storms observed from our web tier (exponential backoff not applied consistently)

We rolled back a local change and warmed caches but the issue persists. Please escalate — our production customers (including two enterprise customers) are impacted.

Thanks,
Emma Davies
CTO, Orchid Labs

------------------------------------------------------------------
From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: support@orchidlabs.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:28:09 -0700
Subject: Re: High 504s starting 06/01 - will need urgent help

Emma — thanks for the quick heads up and the traces. I'm escalating to infra and the on-call runtime team now. Initial ask: can you confirm if the 504s are predominantly coming from a particular endpoint or model route? Also, did you see any client-side retries stack up in the same minute windows as the server 504 spikes?

We've seen similar symptom patterns in the past related to KV cache eviction/race behavior under a tight batch window. I'm adding Rishi (runtime) and Monica (Customer Success) so we can coordinate a mitigation plan.

-Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

------------------------------------------------------------------
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:42:35 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 504s starting 06/01 - will need urgent help

Spinning up investigation notes:
- I pulled the traces and logs (orchid_sample_logs.json). We're seeing a pattern where batch coalescence attempts are queuing requests while the KV cache returns partial entries. The runtime then tries to rebuild KV prefixes which triggers extra batching rounds — effectively a feedback loop.
- Under a sudden spike in warm-start requests, the cache eviction policy looks to be thrashing on a small hot-prefix set which causes sustained queueing for 2-5s per token generation attempt. That maps to the 3s p99 you reported.
- I'm going to push an immediate mitigation: reduce the batch coalescence window for Orchid's model route by 50% and force-prefix-cache-accept on the most common prefixes. This should cut the extra queuing rounds.

Immediate action items (internal):
1) Deploy batch window reduction on the dedicated routing rule for Orchid (connor/rishi).
2) Disable aggressive prefix prefetching for the next 30m (ops).
3) Contact Orchid and ask for a temporary client retry cooldown (Monica to coordinate).

I'll start the deploy now and monitor. If the feedback persists we'll open a hotfix for the KV eviction ordering.

-Rishi
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

------------------------------------------------------------------
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: support@orchidlabs.com, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:05:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 504s starting 06/01 - will need urgent help

Emma — thanks for providing the logs. We're applying an interim mitigation now (batch window reduced; prefix prefetch disabled). Can you please temporarily stop client retries for the next 20 minutes or apply a conservative backoff? That will help the runtime drain and avoid further amplification.

If you can't pause retries across all clients, please at least throttle the high-volume web tier (we can provide a suggested backoff config). I'll stay on this and message you as we see improvements.

-Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

------------------------------------------------------------------
From: support@orchidlabs.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:23:49 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 504s starting 06/01 - will need urgent help

Monica — we've temporarily disabled the aggressive client retry policy on the web tier and applied a 1s jittered backoff. Initial numbers look better: error rate down to ~1.9% and p99 latency falling to ~600ms. We'll leave it paused while you monitor. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Emma

------------------------------------------------------------------
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: emma.davies@orchidlabs.com, procurement@orchidlabs.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 17:42:10 -07:00
Subject: Executive summary: Orchid Labs outage window and next steps

Team — quick exec summary for the customer and internal stakeholders:
- Incident summary: transient cache eviction + batch coalescence feedback loop caused request queueing and 504 spikes for ~50 minutes (2027-06-01 07:50–08:40 PDT).
- Impact: p99 latency up to 3.2s, 504/5xx rate peaked at 8%, customer-reported client retry amplification contributed to the severity.
- Mitigation performed: reduced batch coalescence window, disabled prefix prefetch for affected route, customer applied temporary retry cooldown — restored service to acceptable levels within ~30 minutes of mitigations.
- Root cause (short): race between KV cache refill and batch coalescer under high burst load exposing an ordering bug in prefix eviction logic.
- Next steps (owners and ETA):
  * Rishi: hotfix for deterministic KV eviction ordering (ETA 72 hours) — runtime team
  * Marissa: coordinate post-incident follow-up meeting with Orchid and provide credits per SLA if requested (ETA 24 hours) — CS/Account
  * Connor: produce a short postmortem and remediation plan for the public API doc (ETA 48 hours) — Solutions
  * Monica: provide recommended client-side retry configuration and a test harness to validate (ETA 48 hours) — CS

Emma/Orchid — please let us know if the timeline above works for you or if you'd prefer faster escalation (we can expedite the hotfix and involve more engineering bandwidth).

Thanks all — excellent cross-team response. I'll run a follow-up call if Orchid wants one.

-Lauren
VP, Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
